Verifier uses {1,8} and {4,7}. So active pairs are 1 and 8; 4 and 7. Rule: For each row, if exactly two colored cells (non-zero) and their colors set in pairs, move right color to left_pos+1. Wait if target != right_pos, output[target]=right_col; output[right_pos]=0. Important: If target == right_pos? then no change, meaning already adjacent? If left_pos+1 == right_pos, no change. If there are gap, move right element left to immediately right of left. So it shifts mobile right element leftwards. In given example row [0,8,0,1] -> [0,8,1,0]: colors 8 and 1, left is 8 at pos1, right is 1 at pos3, target pos2, move 1 to pos2, pos3 becomes 0.

Need produce demonstration pairs. Student sees only pairs. We should provide diverse examples illustrating rule: rows with active pairs, all orientations for each pair. Colors 1/8 and 4/7. Also inactive rows with other colors or single color, pairs separated by gap/adjoining, multiple rows, rectangular dimensions. But must consider verifier condition: It only processes if len(colored)==2 for row. If row has more than 2 colored cells, even if contains pair plus other color, it does nothing. Natural language says "In some rows both members of a pair appear, separated by one or more empty cells... Other colors may also appear..." But verifier restricts exactly two colored nonzero. The natural language says "Colored cells are sparse, with at most one of each color per row." It doesn't explicitly say exactly two. However verifier: len(colored)==2. This is a crucial discrepancy. We need teach Student based on verifier outputs, so include pairs with exactly two to show transformations. Should we include rows with 3+ colored cells where a pair exists to show they remain unchanged? The verifier would leave them unchanged. That would be important for Student to infer the exact condition. But if we include many 3-color rows, Student might think pairs don't operate when other colors present. We should definitely include such negative examples to distinguish. Also rows with active pair plus background gap.

Need call show_transformed_input with input grids. Only one call per input? tool takes one input grid and computes output. We can include multiple pairs maybe one grid per call. Better to create a few grids, each containing multiple rows, demonstrating various aspects.

This demonstrates both pairs both orders.

Row1: [0,4,0,7] -> left4 pos1 right7 pos3 target2 -> output [0,4,7,0]
